chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ali from the two (Imams) from Ibn Muskan from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked: 'What is the ruling for one performing Tamattu' who had intercourse with his wife before shaving (qasr)? He said: 'He should slaughter a camel.'

key_terms.جَزُوراً: A mature camel, the specific animal prescribed for this expiation
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٌ: A pilgrim performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرْ: To shave or trim the hair of the head, a key ritual act concluding Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for having intercourse before shaving during Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq, the penalty for premature intimacy during Hajj al-Tamattu' is specified as slaughtering a camel (jazur), reflecting the severity of the breach before the final rites. This ruling is distinct from the general fidyah options in Surah Al-Baqarah, highlighting the specific jurisprudential application within the Shia tradition regarding the timing of the act relative to the completion of the pilgrimage rituals.
